title: embeddings-rerank-debug-scratch-liam-chen-2026-03-04
content:
Context:
- Reranking endpoint started returning high P95 latency for a subset of requests (~2026-03-03 22:00 UTC).
- Observed increased error rate: dimension mismatch errors and occasional fallbacks to CPU path causing long tails.
- Likely correlated with a model rollout that happened ~2026-03-03 21:45 (small canary).

What I saw (quick hits):
- Error in app logs: "ValueError: embedding dimension mismatch: expected 1536, got 512" for request_id=req_8f7a
- Rerank service trace shows immediate prevalidation failure, then synchronous fallback to older rerank model which is served on CPU -> spike in latency (p95 from 120ms -> 2.4s)
- A small % of requests succeed with 1536-dim embeddings, others with 512-dim. Pattern appears by client model tag in request metadata.

Hypothesis summary:
1) Model-catalog mislabel: a new embedding model (512d) was added and labeled incorrectly in the routing table as "text-embed-384/1536" causing downstream consumers to expect 1536d.
2) Client SDK started shipping a different model id (or fallback) for some tenants after feature-flag change.
3) Inconsistent caching: prefix cache or KV cache storing old-dim vectors and being returned for some queries due to cache key normalization bug.
4) Canary rollout imbalance: canary routing returned 512d to some customers while the reranker still expects 1536d.

Commands / probes I ran:
- Get recent logs around failure:
  gcloud logging read "resource.type=cloud_run AND textPayload:embedding dimension mismatch" --limit 50 --project=redwood-inference --freshness=1d

- Tail rerank service logs (k8s):
  kubectl -n prod logs -l app=rerank-service --since=2h | grep -i "dimension mismatch" -n

- Inspect model-catalog entry for text-embedding-*:
  curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://internal-api.redwood/model-catalog/models | jq '.[] | select(.id|test("embed"))' | grep -A4 -E "id|dimensions|tags"
  => found model id embed-serializer-v2 -> dimensions: 512 (suspicious)

- Replayed a failing request locally (python snippet):
  import requests
  payload = {
    "query": "best restaurants near me",
    "top_k": 10,
    "embedding": [/* truncated */],
  }
  r = requests.post('https://api.redwood/re-rank', json=payload, headers={ 'x-request-id': 'debug-replay-01' })
  print(r.status_code, r.text)
  # got 400 + ValueError: embedding dimension mismatch: expected 1536, got 512

- Quick sanity: call embedding endpoint that client uses:
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood/embeddings -d '{"input":"hello"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLIENT_TOKEN" | jq -r '.data[0].embedding | length'
  => returned 512 for some tokens, 1536 for others depending on header x-model-id

- Check routing table / feature flags:
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://internal-api.redwood/route-configs/embeddings | jq .
  => suspect: route config contains an entry mapping product-tier B to model-id embed-serializer-v2 (512) while rerank expects embed-text-xl (1536)

Logs / error snippets (copied):
- 2026-03-03T21:58:12Z [ERROR] rerank-service req=req_8f7a prevalidate: ValueError: embedding dimension mismatch: expected=1536 got=512
- 2026-03-03T22:03:07Z [WARN] rerank-service req=req_9c3b fallback_to_cpu=true backend_latency_ms=2418
- 2026-03-03T22:15:44Z [INFO] embeddings-service req=req_ab12 returned model=embed-serializer-v2 dims=512 runtime=12ms

Initial root-cause leads:
- Model rollout (embed-serializer-v2, 512d) was rolled to canary with tag "canary-embed-2026-03-03" and a misconfigured routing rule assigned it to a subset of tenants but did not update the rerank prevalidation matrix.
- The rerank prevalidation is schema-driven and expects specific dims by model family id; the new model id wasn't added and default expectation stayed 1536 -> raises error and falls back.

Short repro steps for eng team:
1) Call embeddings endpoint with x-model-id: embed-serializer-v2 -> returns 512d.
2) Send same embedding payload to rerank endpoint -> observe ValueError (expected 1536).
3) Toggle feature-flag routing to send embed-serializer-v2 to the same tenant -> observe higher p95 and CPU fallback logs.

Mitigation options tried/notes:
- Temporarily set rerank prevalidation to be tolerant (accept 512 or 1536) -> requires a quick patch, risky for model semantics. (Not yet deployed)
- Rollback canary of embed-serializer-v2: opened PR to ops (see linked_artifacts) -> pending approval (impact: loss of canary testing)
- Add immediate alert: error rate for "embedding dimension mismatch" -> pager created (alert id: ENG-ALERT-732)

Next action checklist (prioritized):
- [ ] Confirm which tenants saw 512d via access logs + correlate with routing table entry (owner: Maya)
- [ ] Rollback embed-serializer-v2 canary or remove tenant mapping in route config if rollout misconfigured (owner: SRE/Release Eng)
- [ ] Add defensive prevalidation change: surface a clear 400 with hint to migrate model dims instead of fallback (owner: eng-serving-runtime)
- [ ] Add unit/integration test for route-config -> prevalidation consistency to CI (owner: eng-applied-ml)
- [ ] Add a migration note in model-catalog describing dimension change and compatibility guidance (owner: product-models)

Observations / random notes to self:
- Some clients have logic to compress embeddings to 512 before sending (bad). Check SDK v2.3.1 release notes for change.
- Batching behavior: when mixed-dimension embeddings enter a batch, the batcher currently chooses the widest dimension and pads/trims others — this is a potential root cause if padding is done incorrectly.
- KV cache keys: we use text normalization + model-id in cache key; if model-id canonicalization changed (e.g., aliasing) two different model-ids could map to same cache key -> corrupted cached values.

Quick reproducer commands to hand to SRE:
- Identify affected requests:
  gcloud logging read 'jsonPayload.message:"embedding dimension mismatch"' --limit 100 --project=redwood-inference --freshness=3d --format='json' | jq -r '.[].jsonPayload' > /tmp/dim-mismatch-sample.json

- Confirm model catalog entry returned dims:
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://internal-api.redwood/model-catalog/models/embed-serializer-v2 | jq '.dimensions'

- Toggle route config for tenant (dry-run):
  curl -X PATCH -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    https://internal-api.redwood/route-configs/embeddings/tenant-123 -d '{"model_id":"embed-text-xl","dry_run":true}'

Notes for post-mortem (if it becomes an incident):
- Timeline of rollout events + who approved canary.
- Why prevalidation didn't include new model id (process gap: model onboarding checklist incomplete).
- Why cached entries could serve mixed dims (if confirmed) -> follow up with caching team.
- Communication: notify affected customers with mitigation steps and ETA for permanent fix.

If you pick this up: start with model-catalog and route-config audit. Correlate logs for req ids listed above (req_8f7a, req_9c3b, req_ab12). Ping Maya/Evelyn if you need the mapping from tenant -> customer-id (they have the mapping export).

-- Liam
